records.source: בִּשְׁנַ֣ת חֲדָ֗ה לְבֵלְאשַׁצַּר֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ בָּבֶ֔ל דָּנִיֵּאל֙ חֵ֣לֶם חֲזָ֔ה וְחֶזְוֵ֥י רֵאשֵׁ֖הּ עַֽל־מִשְׁכְּבֵ֑הּ בֵּאדַ֨יִן֙ חֶלְמָ֣א כְתַ֔ב רֵ֥אשׁ מִלִּ֖ין אֲמַֽר׃
records.gloss: In year one of Belshazzar king of Babylon, Daniel saw a dream and visions of his head upon his bed; then the dream he wrote; [the] head of [the] matters he told.
pieces: In the first year of Belshazzar's reign over Babylon, Daniel had a dream, and as he lay in bed, visions came into his mind. Then he wrote the dream down and gave an account of the main things in it.

L.1: In the first year of Belshazzar king of Babylon, Daniel saw a dream and visions of his head, lying on his bed. Then he wrote the dream down; he told the sum of the matters.

R.1: In Belshazzar's first year as king of Babylon, Daniel had a dream. As he lay on his bed, he saw visions in his mind. Then he wrote the dream down and told the most important parts of it.

decisions.choice: the first year of Belshazzar: some years before the fall of Babylon told in chapter 5
decisions.reason: Belshazzar was the son of Nabonidus, the last king of Babylon, and ruled in Babylon while his father stayed away in Arabia, from about 550 BC. Babylon fell to the Persians in 539 BC, on the night told in chapter 5. So this chapter, and chapter 8 (dated in Belshazzar's third year), go back in time before chapters 5 and 6. The book arranges its visions in their own order, after the stories.

decisions.choice: the vision is still written in Aramaic
decisions.reason: The Aramaic that began at 2:4 runs on through this chapter to 7:28. The vision of four beasts stands in the same language as Nebuchadnezzar's dream of a statue made of four metals (chapter 2), and the two chapters, which both tell of four kingdoms followed by God's kingdom, frame the Aramaic part of the book. The book returns to Hebrew at 8:1.

decisions.choice: visions of his head: visions that passed through his mind
decisions.reason: The "head" is where dreams and thoughts are seen, as in 2:28 and 4:2, 7. Daniel saw these things in a dream at night, as he lay asleep.

decisions.choice: he told the head of the matters: he gave the substance of what he saw
alternatives: the beginning of the account; he said:
decisions.reason: The "head" of the matters is their chief part or sum. The last verb is the ordinary word "said", used here for telling the account. It may also introduce what follows: "the beginning of the account, he said". Either way, verses 2-28 are Daniel's own account in his own words.

decisions.choice: in the first year of Belshazzar's reign (B); in Belshazzar's first year as king (R)
decisions.reason: The date follows the wording set for dated headings in Jeremiah. Balanced and Readable say that the visions were in his mind (m3), and Readable divides the long sentence.

records.heading: Four beasts from the sea

records.source: עָנֵ֤ה דָנִיֵּאל֙ וְאָמַ֔ר חָזֵ֥ה הֲוֵ֛ית בְּחֶזְוִ֖י עִם־לֵֽילְיָ֑א וַאֲר֗וּ אַרְבַּע֙ רוּחֵ֣י שְׁמַיָּ֔א מְגִיחָ֖ן לְיַמָּ֥א רַבָּֽא׃
records.gloss: Answering Daniel and saying, seeing I was in my vision with the night, and look, four [the] winds of the heavens stirring up the sea the great.
pieces: Daniel said: In my vision at night I looked, and I saw the four winds of heaven churning up the great sea.

L.2: Daniel answered and said: I was looking in my vision by night, and look, the four winds of the heavens were stirring up the great sea.

R.2: This is what Daniel said: In my vision during the night, I saw strong winds blowing from every direction. They were stirring up the great sea.

decisions.choice: answered and said: began to speak
decisions.reason: The pair of verbs is a common way of introducing speech in the Aramaic of Daniel (2:5; 3:14). There is no question being answered. From here on Daniel tells the vision in his own words, in the first person.

decisions.choice: I was looking: I kept watching, over a span of time
decisions.reason: The participle with the verb "to be" describes looking that went on. The same phrase marks each new step of the vision (verses 4, 6, 7, 9, 11, 13, 21).

decisions.choice: the four winds of heaven stirring up the great sea: storms from every side whipping up the sea
decisions.reason: The four winds are the winds from the four directions, so the whole sky. The great sea may be the Mediterranean, which has that name (Numbers 34:6), but in the vision it is the restless deep, which in Hebrew poetry stands for the forces that oppose God (Isaiah 17:12-13; 27:1; Psalm 74:13). The beasts come up out of it.

decisions.choice: look (L); I saw (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "look", the word that marks something seen in a vision, as in Zechariah. Balanced and Readable say "I saw". Readable says "strong winds blowing from every direction" for the four winds (m3), and Daniel's account is not set in quotation marks, since it runs on as his own telling of the vision to the end of the chapter.

records.source: וְאַרְבַּ֤ע חֵיוָן֙ רַבְרְבָ֔ן סָלְקָ֖ן מִן־יַמָּ֑א שָׁנְיָ֖ן דָּ֥א מִן־דָּֽא׃
records.gloss: And four beasts great coming up from the sea, different this from this.
pieces: Four huge beasts rose out of the sea, each unlike the others.

L.3: And four great beasts were coming up from the sea, different from one another.

R.3: Four huge animals came up out of the sea. Each one was different from the others.

decisions.choice: four great beasts from the sea: taken up in Revelation 13
decisions.reason: Revelation 13:1-2 sees one beast rising from the sea with ten horns, like a leopard, with feet like a bear's and a mouth like a lion's: the four beasts of Daniel 7 joined in one. Verse 17 says that the beasts are four kings.

decisions.choice: animals (R)
decisions.reason: Readable says "animals" for "beasts"; the word is the ordinary word for a wild animal.

records.source: קַדְמָיְתָ֣א כְאַרְיֵ֔ה וְגַפִּ֥ין דִּֽי־נְשַׁ֖ר לַ֑הּ חָזֵ֣ה הֲוֵ֡ית עַד֩ דִּי־מְּרִ֨יטוּ גַפַּ֜יהּ וּנְטִ֣ילַת מִן־אַרְעָ֗א וְעַל־רַגְלַ֨יִן֙ כֶּאֱנָ֣שׁ הֳקִימַ֔ת וּלְבַ֥ב אֱנָ֖שׁ יְהִ֥יב לַֽהּ׃
records.gloss: The first [was] like a lion, and wings of an eagle [were] to it; seeing I was until that were plucked off its wings, and it was lifted up from the earth and on two feet like a man it was made to stand, and a heart of a man was given to it.
pieces: The first was like a lion, and it had eagle's wings. As I watched, its wings were torn off, and it was lifted from the ground and set on two feet like a human being, and it was given a human mind.

L.4: The first was like a lion and had the wings of an eagle. I kept looking until its wings were plucked off, and it was lifted from the earth and set upright on two feet like a human, and a human heart was given to it.

R.4: The first animal looked like a lion, but it had wings like an eagle. As I watched, its wings were pulled off. It was lifted off the ground and made to stand up on two feet like a person. It was given a human mind.

decisions.choice: a lion with eagle's wings: the usual reading is the kingdom of Babylon
decisions.reason: Glazed lions lined the processional way of Babylon, winged lions are common in the art of Mesopotamia, and the prophets compare Nebuchadnezzar to a lion and an eagle (Jeremiah 4:7; 49:19, 22; Ezekiel 17:3). The first part of the statue in chapter 2, the head of gold, is Babylon (2:38). The vision itself names no kingdom.

decisions.choice: made to stand like a human, given a human heart: a beast made humane
decisions.reason: The lion is humbled and then given a human heart, the reverse of what happened to Nebuchadnezzar, who was given the heart of an animal until he acknowledged the Most High (4:13, 31-33). Many readers see his story behind this picture.

decisions.choice: a human heart: a human mind and understanding
decisions.reason: In Aramaic as in Hebrew the heart is the seat of thinking and will, not chiefly of feeling (4:13).

decisions.choice: like a human; a human heart (L); a human mind (B, R)
decisions.reason: The word means a human being, not a male, so every level says "human" or "person". Balanced and Readable say "mind" for heart (m3).

records.source: וַאֲר֣וּ חֵיוָה֩ אָחֳרִ֨י תִנְיָנָ֜ה דָּמְיָ֣ה לְדֹ֗ב וְלִשְׂטַר־חַד֙ הֳקִמַ֔ת וּתְלָ֥ת עִלְעִ֛ין בְּפֻמַּ֖הּ בֵּ֣ין שִׁנַּ֑הּ וְכֵן֙ אָמְרִ֣ין לַ֔הּ ק֥וּמִֽי אֲכֻ֖לִי בְּשַׂ֥ר שַׂגִּֽיא׃
records.gloss: And look, a beast another, a second, resembling a bear, and to a side one it was raised, and three ribs [were] in its mouth between its teeth, and thus [they were] saying to it: Arise, devour flesh much.
pieces: Then I saw another beast, a second one, that looked like a bear. It was raised up on one side, and it had three ribs in its mouth between its teeth. It was told, "Get up and eat your fill of flesh!"

L.5: And look, another beast, a second one, like a bear. It was raised on one side, with three ribs in its mouth between its teeth; and thus they were saying to it, "Arise, devour much flesh."

R.5: Then I saw a second animal. It looked like a bear. It was raised up on one side, and it had three ribs in its mouth between its teeth. Someone told it, "Get up and eat as much meat as you want!"

decisions.choice: raised up on one side: rearing up on one side, or with one side higher
decisions.reason: The picture may be of a bear lifting itself on one side, ready to spring, or of a body higher on one side than the other. The usual reading of the second kingdom as Media, or as Media and Persia, has taken it as the stronger Persian side of a joint empire (8:3, 20). The vision does not explain it.

decisions.choice: a bear with three ribs in its mouth: a second kingdom that devours others
decisions.reason: The ribs are the remains of prey. They are usually read as three lands it has conquered. The second kingdom is read as Media (in the reading that takes the four kingdoms as Babylon, Media, Persia and Greece) or as Medo-Persia (in the reading that takes them as Babylon, Medo-Persia, Greece and Rome); see verse 17.

decisions.choice: thus they were saying to it: it was told
decisions.reason: The plural verb has no stated subject. In the Aramaic of Daniel this is a common way of saying that something was said or done without naming who did it (4:22, 29). The command to devour comes from heaven, where the kingdoms are given their power.

decisions.choice: It was told (B); Someone told it (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "they were saying"; Balanced and Readable say it without an unnamed "they" (m3).

records.source: בָּאתַ֨ר דְּנָ֜ה חָזֵ֣ה הֲוֵ֗ית וַאֲר֤וּ אָֽחֳרִי֙ כִּנְמַ֔ר וְלַ֨הּ גַּפִּ֥ין אַרְבַּ֛ע דִּי־ע֖וֹף עַל־גַּבַּ֑הּ וְאַרְבְּעָ֤ה רֵאשִׁין֙ לְחֵ֣יוְתָ֔א וְשָׁלְטָ֖ן יְהִ֥יב לַֽהּ׃
records.gloss: After this seeing I was, and look, another, like a leopard, and to it wings four of a bird upon its back, and four heads [were] to the beast, and dominion was given to it.
pieces: After that, as I watched, I saw another beast, like a leopard. On its back it had four wings like a bird's, and the beast had four heads. It was given authority to rule.

L.6: After this I kept looking, and look, another, like a leopard, and it had four wings of a bird on its back; and the beast had four heads, and dominion was given to it.

R.6: After that, I saw another animal. It looked like a leopard, and it had four wings like a bird's on its back. This animal had four heads, and it was given power to rule.

decisions.choice: a leopard with four wings and four heads: a swift kingdom
decisions.reason: The leopard is fast, and the wings make it faster. In the reading that takes the four kingdoms as Babylon, Media, Persia and Greece, it is Persia, whose four kings are named in 11:2; in the reading that takes them as Babylon, Medo-Persia, Greece and Rome, it is Greece, whose empire was divided among four after Alexander (8:8, 22). The vision does not name it; see verse 17.

decisions.choice: dominion was given to it: it was allowed to rule
decisions.reason: The passive verb, as in verse 4, implies that God gives each kingdom its rule (2:21, 37; 4:14).

decisions.choice: authority to rule (B); power to rule (R)
decisions.reason: The noun means rule or dominion. Balanced and Readable use plain words for it here and in verses 12, 14, 26 and 27; Literal keeps "dominion".

records.source: בָּאתַ֣ר דְּנָה֩ חָזֵ֨ה הֲוֵ֜ית בְּחֶזְוֵ֣י לֵֽילְיָ֗א וַאֲר֣וּ חֵיוָ֣ה רְֽבִיעָאָ֡ה דְּחִילָה֩ וְאֵֽימְתָנִ֨י וְתַקִּיפָ֜א יַתִּ֗ירָא וְשִׁנַּ֨יִן דִּֽי־פַרְזֶ֥ל לַהּ֙ רַבְרְבָ֔ן אָֽכְלָ֣ה וּמַדֱּקָ֔ה וּשְׁאָרָ֖א בְּרַגְלַ֣הּ רָפְסָ֑ה וְהִ֣יא מְשַׁנְּיָ֗ה מִן־כָּל־חֵֽיוָתָא֙ דִּ֣י קָֽדָמַ֔יהּ וְקַרְנַ֥יִן עֲשַׂ֖ר לַֽהּ׃
records.gloss: After this seeing I was in visions of the night, and look, a beast fourth, dreadful and terrible and strong exceedingly, and teeth of iron [were] to it, great; [it was] devouring and crushing, and the rest with its feet trampling; and it [was] different from all the beasts that [were] before it, and horns ten [were] to it.
pieces: After that, in my visions at night, I saw a fourth beast, terrifying, frightening and very strong. It had huge iron teeth. It devoured and crushed its victims, and trampled what was left under its feet. It was unlike all the beasts before it, and it had ten horns.

L.7: After this I kept looking in the visions of the night, and look, a fourth beast, dreadful and terrible and exceedingly strong. It had great teeth of iron; it was devouring and crushing, and trampling what was left with its feet. It was different from all the beasts that came before it, and it had ten horns.

R.7: After that, in my visions during the night, I saw a fourth animal. It was terrifying and frightening and very strong. It had huge teeth made of iron. It ate and crushed its victims, and it stamped on whatever was left. It was not like any of the animals before it, and it had ten horns.

decisions.choice: the fourth beast: not like any known animal
decisions.reason: Daniel compares the first three beasts to a lion, a bear and a leopard, but the fourth he can only describe. Its iron teeth recall the legs of iron of the statue in chapter 2, the fourth kingdom that crushes all the others (2:40). Verse 23 says it is a fourth kingdom. In the reading that takes the four kingdoms as Babylon, Media, Persia and Greece, it is the Greek kingdom of Alexander and his successors; in the reading that takes them as Babylon, Medo-Persia, Greece and Rome, it is Rome. See verse 17.

decisions.choice: ten horns: ten kings (verse 24)
decisions.reason: A horn is an animal's strength, and so stands for a king's power (8:20-22; Zechariah 2:1-4). The angel explains the ten horns as ten kings who arise from this kingdom (verse 24).

decisions.choice: a beast with ten horns: Revelation 12:3; 13:1; 17:3, 12
decisions.reason: Revelation gives ten horns to the dragon and to the beast from the sea, and explains them, as Daniel's angel does, as ten kings (Revelation 17:12).

decisions.choice: its victims (B, R)
decisions.reason: The Aramaic leaves the object of devouring and crushing to be understood; Balanced and Readable supply "its victims".

records.source: מִשְׂתַּכַּ֨ל הֲוֵ֜ית בְּקַרְנַיָּ֗א וַ֠אֲלוּ קֶ֣רֶן אָחֳרִ֤י זְעֵירָה֙ סִלְקָ֣ת בֵּֽינֵיהֵ֔ן וּתְלָ֗ת מִן־קַרְנַיָּא֙ קַדְמָ֣יָתָ֔א אֶתְעֲקַ֖רָה מִן־קֳדָמַ֑הּ וַאֲל֨וּ עַיְנִ֜ין כְּעַיְנֵ֤י אֲנָשָׁא֙ בְּקַרְנָא־דָ֔א וּפֻ֖ם מְמַלִּ֥ל רַבְרְבָֽן׃
records.gloss: Considering I was the horns, and look, a horn another, small, came up between them, and three of the horns the first were uprooted from before it; and look, eyes like eyes of a man [were] in the horn this, and a mouth speaking great [things].
pieces: While I was studying the horns, another horn, a small one, grew up among them, and three of the earlier horns were pulled up by the roots to make room for it. This horn had eyes like a human's eyes and a mouth that spoke boastfully.

L.8: I was considering the horns, and look, another horn, a small one, came up among them, and three of the former horns were uprooted before it. And look, in this horn were eyes like human eyes, and a mouth speaking great things.

R.8: While I was thinking about the horns, I saw another horn come up among them. It was a small horn. Three of the first horns were pulled out to make room for it. This small horn had eyes like a person's eyes, and it had a mouth that was boasting.

decisions.choice: the small horn: a king who rises from the fourth kingdom (verses 24-25)
decisions.reason: The angel explains the horn as a king who comes after the ten, brings down three, speaks against the Most High and persecutes the holy ones (verses 24-25). In the reading that takes the fourth kingdom as Greece, he is usually identified with Antiochus IV Epiphanes, the Seleucid king who persecuted the Jews in 167-164 BC, as the small horn of 8:9 is. Christian tradition has often read him as a final enemy of God at the end of history (compare 2 Thessalonians 2:3-4). The text names no one.

decisions.choice: a mouth speaking great things: boasting, arrogant speech
decisions.reason: "Great things" are proud claims. Verse 25 says that he will speak against the Most High. Revelation 13:5 gives the beast "a mouth speaking great things and blasphemies".

decisions.choice: eyes like human eyes: intelligence and watchfulness
decisions.reason: The eyes set this horn apart from the others as shrewd and watchful. The angel does not explain them; 8:23 speaks of a king "skilled in intrigue".

decisions.choice: spoke boastfully (B); was boasting (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "speaking great things"; Balanced and Readable say what it means (m2). Readable says "pulled out" for the uprooted horns.

records.source: חָזֵ֣ה הֲוֵ֗ית עַ֣ד דִּ֤י כָרְסָוָן֙ רְמִ֔יו וְעַתִּ֥יק יוֹמִ֖ין יְתִ֑ב לְבוּשֵׁ֣הּ׀כִּתְלַ֣ג חִוָּ֗ר וּשְׂעַ֤ר רֵאשֵׁהּ֙ כַּעֲמַ֣ר נְקֵ֔א כָּרְסְיֵהּ֙ שְׁבִיבִ֣ין דִּי־נ֔וּר גַּלְגִּלּ֖וֹהִי נ֥וּר דָּלִֽק׃
records.gloss: Seeing I was until that thrones were placed, and [one] ancient of days sat; his clothing like snow white, and [the] hair of his head like wool pure; his throne [was] flames of fire, its wheels fire burning.
pieces: As I watched, thrones were put in place, \q and the Ancient of Days was seated. \q His clothes were white as snow, and the hair of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} head like clean wool. \q His throne was flames of fire, \q and its wheels were blazing fire.

L.9: I kept looking until thrones were put in place, \q and the Ancient of Days sat down. \q His garment was white like snow, and the hair of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} head like clean wool; \q {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} throne was flames of fire, \q its wheels burning fire.

R.9: As I watched, thrones were set up, \q and the Ancient One sat down on {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} throne. \q His clothes were as white as snow, and the hair on {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} head was like clean wool. \q His throne was made of flames of fire, \q and its wheels were burning with fire.

decisions.choice: the Ancient of Days: God, pictured as an aged judge on his throne
decisions.reason: The words mean "one advanced in days", an old man. They are a description, not a name: there is no article in 7:9, and the same figure is called "the Ancient of Days" in verses 13 and 22. In the scene he is the judge on the throne, served by thousands (verse 10), and verse 22 shows that he gives the kingdom to the holy ones of the Most High. Age here stands for wisdom, authority and endless life. He is God, though the vision does not use the name.

decisions.choice: white clothing and hair like wool: purity and great age
decisions.reason: White clothes are a sign of purity and of heavenly glory, and white hair a sign of age and honor (Proverbs 16:31). Revelation 1:14 gives the same white hair, like wool and snow, to the risen Jesus.

decisions.choice: a throne of fire with wheels: the chariot-throne of Ezekiel 1 and 10
decisions.reason: Ezekiel saw God's throne above wheels and living creatures, with fire flashing among them (Ezekiel 1:13-27; 10:2-6). Fire in the Bible is a sign of God's holy presence and of judgment (Exodus 19:18; Deuteronomy 4:24).

decisions.choice: thrones were set in place: for the court that sits in verse 10
decisions.reason: The thrones are set for the judgment. Verse 10 says that "the court sat". The text does not say who sits on the other thrones; heavenly beings sit with God in judgment elsewhere (1 Kings 22:19; Psalm 89:8). Revelation 4:4 and 20:4 also picture thrones around God's throne.

decisions.choice: verses 9-10 set in lines; the Ancient of Days (L, B), the Ancient One (R); his (deity pronoun)
decisions.reason: The terms note sets 7:9-10 and 13-14 in lines: they are a poem in rhythmic lines within the vision. Daniel's own telling, not a quotation, so no quotation marks. The title follows the table for Daniel: "the Ancient of Days" at Literal and Balanced and "the Ancient One" at Readable. Pronouns for him are the pronouns for God, with the capitalized form as a setting.

records.source: נְהַ֣ר דִּי־נ֗וּר נָגֵ֤ד וְנָפֵק֙ מִן־קֳדָמ֔וֹהִי אֶ֤לֶף אַלְפִין֙ יְשַׁמְּשׁוּנֵּ֔הּ וְרִבּ֥וֹ רִבְבָ֖ן קָֽדָמ֣וֹהִי יְקוּמ֑וּן דִּינָ֥א יְתִ֖ב וְסִפְרִ֥ין פְּתִֽיחוּ׃
records.gloss: A river of fire [was] flowing and coming out from before him; a thousand thousands were serving him, and a myriad myriads before him were standing; the court sat, and books were opened.
pieces: A river of fire was streaming out, flowing from {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} presence. \q Thousands upon thousands served {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, \q and countless thousands stood before {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. \q The court was seated, and the books were opened.

L.10: A river of fire was flowing and coming out from before {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}; \q a thousand thousands were serving {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, \q and ten thousand times ten thousand were standing before {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. \q The court sat, and books were opened.

R.10: A river of fire was flowing out from in front of {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. \q Thousands and thousands of servants served {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. \q Millions of them stood in front of {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. \q The court began its work, and the books were opened.

decisions.choice: a thousand thousands, a myriad of myriads: a number past counting
decisions.reason: A myriad is ten thousand. The numbers are not meant to be added up: they say that God's attendants are beyond counting. Revelation 5:11 describes the angels around the throne in the same words.

decisions.choice: the court sat: the heavenly court took its seats for judgment
decisions.reason: The word means judgment, and here the court that gives it. It sits again in verse 26, where the small horn's rule is taken away.

decisions.choice: books were opened: the records of what people have done
decisions.reason: The books are the record by which the court judges. Compare 12:1, where the names of God's people are written in a book, and Revelation 20:12, where "books were opened" and the dead are judged by what is written in them.

decisions.choice: Thousands upon thousands; countless thousands (B); Thousands and thousands; Millions (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Aramaic numbers. Balanced and Readable give their sense, a host past counting (m1). Readable adds "of servants" so that it is clear these are attendants, and says "began its work" for "sat".

decisions.choice: him, his (deity pronoun)
decisions.reason: These pronouns refer to the Ancient of Days and take the deity_pronoun setting. Balanced says "from his presence" for "from before him".

records.source: חָזֵ֣ה הֲוֵ֔ית בֵּאדַ֗יִן מִן־קָל֙ מִלַּיָּ֣א רַבְרְבָתָ֔א דִּ֥י קַרְנָ֖א מְמַלֱּלָ֑ה חָזֵ֣ה הֲוֵ֡ית עַד֩ דִּ֨י קְטִילַ֤ת חֵֽיוְתָא֙ וְהוּבַ֣ד גִּשְׁמַ֔הּ וִיהִיבַ֖ת לִיקֵדַ֥ת אֶשָּֽׁא׃
records.gloss: Seeing I was then, because of [the] sound of the words the great that the horn [was] speaking; seeing I was until that was killed the beast, and was destroyed its body, and it was given to [the] burning of the fire.
pieces: I kept watching because of the boastful words the horn was speaking. As I watched, the beast was put to death, and its body was destroyed and thrown into the blazing fire.

L.11: I kept looking then because of the sound of the great words that the horn was speaking. I kept looking until the beast was killed, and its body was destroyed and given over to the burning fire.

R.11: I kept watching because the horn was still speaking those boastful words. As I watched, the fourth animal was killed. Its body was destroyed and thrown into the fire to burn.

decisions.choice: because of the sound of the great words: Daniel keeps watching because the horn goes on boasting
alternatives: I kept looking from the time of the sound of the great words ...
decisions.reason: The first "I kept looking" stands on its own, and the rest gives the reason: the horn's arrogant words held his attention. Some take the words with what follows: he watched, from the time the horn spoke, until the beast was slain. The sense is close either way: the boasting goes on to the very moment of judgment.

decisions.choice: the beast killed and given to the fire: the end of the fourth kingdom
decisions.reason: The fourth beast is destroyed outright, unlike the others (verse 12). Revelation 19:20 has the beast and the false prophet thrown alive into the lake of fire.

decisions.choice: the fourth animal (R)
decisions.reason: Readable says which beast is meant; the context shows it is the fourth, which bears the horn.

records.source: וּשְׁאָר֙ חֵֽיוָתָ֔א הֶעְדִּ֖יו שָׁלְטָנְה֑וֹן וְאַרְכָ֧ה בְחַיִּ֛ין יְהִ֥יבַת לְה֖וֹן עַד־זְמַ֥ן וְעִדָּֽן׃
records.gloss: And the rest of the beasts, they removed their dominion, and a lengthening in life was given to them until a season and a time.
pieces: The other beasts had their authority taken away, but they were allowed to go on living for a set period of time.

L.12: And the rest of the beasts: their dominion was removed, but a lengthening of life was given to them for a season and a time.

R.12: The other animals had their power to rule taken away. But they were allowed to live on for a while.

decisions.choice: they removed: their dominion was taken away
decisions.reason: As in verse 5, a plural verb with no subject says that something was done without naming who did it.

decisions.choice: for a season and a time: for a set time, fixed by God
decisions.reason: The two words are near synonyms and together mean a period that God has appointed. The earlier kingdoms lose their power, but their peoples go on for a while; only the fourth beast is destroyed (verse 11). Compare 2:21: God "changes times and seasons".

decisions.choice: for a set period of time (B); for a while (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "for a season and a time"; Balanced and Readable give its sense (m2).

records.source: חָזֵ֤ה הֲוֵית֙ בְּחֶזְוֵ֣י לֵֽילְיָ֔א וַאֲרוּ֙ עִם־עֲנָנֵ֣י שְׁמַיָּ֔א כְּבַ֥ר אֱנָ֖שׁ אָתֵ֣ה הֲוָ֑ה וְעַד־עַתִּ֤יק יֽוֹמַיָּא֙ מְטָ֔ה וּקְדָמ֖וֹהִי הַקְרְבֽוּהִי׃
records.gloss: Seeing I was in [the] visions of the night, and look, with [the] clouds of the heavens [one] like a son of man was coming; and to the ancient of days he reached, and before him they brought him near.
pieces: As I watched in the visions of the night, \q I saw one like a son of man \q coming with the clouds of heaven. \q He came to the Ancient of Days \q and was presented before {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

L.13: I kept looking in the visions of the night, \q and look, with the clouds of the heavens \q [one] like a son of man was coming, \q and he reached the Ancient of Days, \q and they brought him close before {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

R.13: As I watched in my visions during the night, \q I saw someone who looked like a human being. \q He was coming with the clouds of the sky. \q He came to the Ancient One \q and was led into {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} presence.

decisions.choice: one like a son of man: a figure in human form
decisions.reason: In Aramaic "son of man" means a human being (4:13, 22; Psalm 8:5). "Like" marks a likeness, as "like a lion" and "like a bear" do in verses 4-5. After four beasts from the sea comes one who looks human, coming with the clouds. The words describe what Daniel saw; they are not yet a title. The figure is not God, since he is brought to the Ancient of Days, and he is kept distinct from him.

decisions.choice: the one like a son of man, the holy ones, and Jesus as the Son of Man
decisions.reason: Three things are true of this verse. First, Jesus takes the phrase as his title "the Son of Man" and speaks of himself as coming with or on the clouds of heaven (Matthew 24:30; 26:64; Mark 13:26; 14:62), and Revelation 1:7 and 1:13 see the risen Jesus in Daniel's words. Second, the angel's explanation in verses 16-27 speaks of the kingdom being given to "the holy ones of the Most High" (verses 18, 22, 27), as it is given here to this figure (verse 14). Third, readers differ on how the two relate: the figure may stand for the holy ones as a group, or be their heavenly leader or representative, or be a messianic king; Jewish and Christian interpreters have read him as the Messiah. The translation keeps the vision's description and does not settle the question.

decisions.choice: coming with the clouds ... to the Ancient of Days: coming into God's presence
decisions.reason: In the vision the figure comes with the clouds to the Ancient of Days, so the movement is toward God's throne, where he receives a kingdom (verse 14). Clouds go with the coming of God himself elsewhere (Psalm 104:3; Isaiah 19:1). Jesus' words before the high priest join this verse to Psalm 110:1 (Mark 14:62).

decisions.choice: [one] like a son of man (L); one like a son of man (B); someone who looked like a human being (R); lowercase, with no deity pronoun
decisions.reason: The wording follows the table for Daniel. Every level keeps it in lowercase, because in the vision it is a description, not a name (m1), and the pronouns for this figure ("he", "him") take no deity_pronoun span, as for the servant in Isaiah. The Ancient of Days and this figure are kept distinct: "before him" at the end of the verse is the Ancient of Days, and that pronoun is God's. Readable gives the meaning of "son of man"; the Gospels' title is explained in m2.

decisions.choice: verses 13-14 set in lines
decisions.reason: The terms note sets 7:13-14 in lines, like 7:9-10. Readable says "led into his presence" for "brought near before him"; that pronoun is the Ancient One's and takes the deity_pronoun setting.

records.source: וְלֵ֨הּ יְהִ֤יב שָׁלְטָן֙ וִיקָ֣ר וּמַלְכ֔וּ וְכֹ֣ל עַֽמְמַיָּ֗א אֻמַיָּ֛א וְלִשָּׁנַיָּ֖א לֵ֣הּ יִפְלְח֑וּן שָׁלְטָנֵ֞הּ שָׁלְטָ֤ן עָלַם֙ דִּֽי־לָ֣א יֶעְדֵּ֔ה וּמַלְכוּתֵ֖הּ דִּי־לָ֥א תִתְחַבַּֽל׃פ
records.gloss: And to him was given dominion and honor and kingdom, and all the peoples, the nations and the languages to him will serve; his dominion [is] a dominion of perpetuity which not will pass away, and his kingdom [one] which not will be destroyed.
pieces: He was given authority, glory and kingly power, \q so that all peoples, nations and languages would serve him. \q His authority is an everlasting authority that will never pass away, \q and his kingdom will never be destroyed.

L.14: And to him were given dominion, glory and a kingdom, \q so that all the peoples, nations and languages would serve him. \q His dominion is an eternal dominion that will not pass away, \q and his kingdom, one that will not be destroyed.

R.14: He was given authority, glory and a kingdom. \q People from every nation and language would serve him. \q His authority will last forever. It will never end. \q His kingdom will never be destroyed.

decisions.choice: dominion, honor and kingdom: the right to rule, the glory that goes with it, and the realm itself
decisions.reason: The same words are used of what God gave Nebuchadnezzar (2:37; 5:18). Now they are given to the one like a son of man, and his rule, unlike the beasts', has no end.

decisions.choice: serve: pay homage and service, as to God
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used in Daniel for serving and worshiping a god (3:12, 14, 17-18, 28; 6:17, 21). Verse 27 uses it for the service all dominions give to the kingdom of the holy ones. It need not mean worship in the full sense, but it is the honor due to God.

decisions.choice: all peoples, nations and languages; an everlasting dominion that will not be destroyed
decisions.reason: The same list of all peoples, nations and languages is used in 3:4 and 6:26 of the empire of Babylon and then Persia. The kingdom that will never be destroyed echoes 2:44 and the praise of God in 4:31 and 6:27. Revelation 11:15 and Luke 1:33 take up the kingdom that has no end.

decisions.choice: him, his, lowercase with no deity pronoun
decisions.reason: These pronouns refer to the one like a son of man, and follow the decision at verse 13: the vision describes him, and the wording does not decide who he is. They take no deity_pronoun span.

decisions.choice: authority (B, R); glory (all levels)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "authority" for dominion, as elsewhere in this chapter. The word for honor ("glory" here) is the one paired with greatness in 4:33 and 5:18.

records.source: אֶתְכְּרִיַּ֥ת רוּחִ֛י אֲנָ֥ה דָנִיֵּ֖אל בְּג֣וֹא נִדְנֶ֑ה וְחֶזְוֵ֥י רֵאשִׁ֖י יְבַהֲלֻנַּֽנִי׃
records.gloss: Was distressed my spirit, I, Daniel, in [the] midst of [its] sheath, and [the] visions of my head alarmed me.
pieces: I, Daniel, was deeply troubled in spirit, and the visions that passed through my mind frightened me.

L.15: As for me, Daniel, my spirit was distressed within its sheath, and the visions of my head alarmed me.

R.15: I, Daniel, was very upset. The visions I saw in my mind frightened me.

decisions.choice: within its sheath: within my body
decisions.reason: The body is pictured as the sheath in which the spirit is kept, as a sword in its sheath. The phrase says that Daniel was troubled inside himself.

decisions.choice: my spirit was distressed: I was deeply disturbed
decisions.reason: The same verb is used of Nebuchadnezzar's troubled spirit after his dream (2:1, 3). Daniel's alarm comes back at the end of the vision (verse 28).

decisions.choice: deeply troubled in spirit (B); very upset (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the picture of the sheath; Balanced and Readable give its sense (m1).

records.heading: The meaning of the vision

records.source: קִרְבֵ֗ת עַל־חַד֙ מִן־קָ֣אֲמַיָּ֔א וְיַצִּיבָ֥א אֶבְעֵֽא־מִנֵּ֖הּ עַֽל־כָּל־דְּנָ֑ה וַאֲמַר־לִ֕י וּפְשַׁ֥ר מִלַּיָּ֖א יְהוֹדְעִנַּֽנִי׃
records.gloss: I approached to one of the standing [ones], and the truth I was asking from him concerning all this; and he said to me, and [the] interpretation of the matters he made known to me:
pieces: I went up to one of those standing there and asked him what all this really meant. So he told me the meaning of these things:

L.16: I went near to one of those standing [there] and asked him the truth about all this. And he told me and made known to me the interpretation of the matters:

R.16: I went to one of the heavenly beings standing there. I asked him to tell me what all this really meant. So he explained it to me. He said,

decisions.choice: one of those standing: one of the heavenly attendants of verse 10
decisions.reason: Those who "stood before him" in verse 10 are the countless attendants of God's court. Daniel goes up to one of them and asks him. In later visions the explaining angel is Gabriel (8:16; 9:21), but this one is not named.

decisions.choice: the truth about all this: what it really means
decisions.reason: "Truth" here is the certain meaning of the vision. The same word comes in verse 19, when Daniel asks to know "the truth" about the fourth beast.

decisions.choice: heavenly beings (R)
decisions.reason: Readable says who the ones standing there are (m1). The angel's words, from verse 17 to verse 18 and again from verse 23 to verse 27, are set in quotation marks at every level, as speech within Daniel's account.

records.source: אִלֵּין֙ חֵיוָתָ֣א רַבְרְבָתָ֔א דִּ֥י אִנִּ֖ין אַרְבַּ֑ע אַרְבְּעָ֥ה מַלְכִ֖ין יְקוּמ֥וּן מִן־אַרְעָֽא׃
records.gloss: These the beasts the great, which they [are] four, four kings [who] will arise from the earth.
pieces: "These four great beasts are four kings who will rise up from the earth.

L.17: "These great beasts, which are four, are four kings who will arise from the earth.

R.17: "These four huge animals are four kings who will come to power on the earth.

decisions.choice: four kings: four kingdoms, most often read as Babylon, Media, Persia and Greece, or as Babylon, Medo-Persia, Greece and Rome
decisions.reason: The angel calls the beasts kings, and in verse 23 he calls the fourth a kingdom: a king stands for his kingdom, as in 2:37-39. The text names only the kingdoms of its own story: Babylon (chapters 1-5), and the Medes and Persians (5:28; 6:9; 8:20) and Greece (8:21). Two main readings have been given. One takes the four as Babylon, Media, Persia and Greece, and the small horn as Antiochus IV, a reading found in some ancient writers and in most modern study. The other, the main Christian reading from early times, takes them as Babylon, Medo-Persia, Greece and Rome. Neither is stated in the text, and the translation does not choose between them.

decisions.choice: who will arise from the earth: kings of this world
decisions.reason: In verse 3 the beasts came up from the sea; here the kings arise from the earth. Both mean the same: they belong to this world, in contrast to the kingdom given from heaven (verses 14, 18). The future tense is spoken from the time of the vision, when the first kingdom was still standing.

decisions.choice: the angel's words in quotation marks
decisions.reason: The angel's explanation is speech within Daniel's account and is set in double quotation marks; it runs to the end of verse 18.

records.source: וִֽיקַבְּלוּן֙ מַלְכוּתָ֔א קַדִּישֵׁ֖י עֶלְיוֹנִ֑ין וְיַחְסְנ֤וּן מַלְכוּתָא֙ עַֽד־עָ֣לְמָ֔א וְעַ֖ד עָלַ֥ם עָלְמַיָּֽא׃
records.gloss: And will receive the kingdom [the] holy ones of [the] Most High, and they will possess the kingdom until perpetuity and until perpetuity of perpetuities.
pieces: But the holy ones of the Most High will receive the kingdom and hold it as their own forever, for ever and ever."

L.18: But the holy ones of the Most High will receive the kingdom, and they will possess the kingdom forever, forever and ever."

R.18: But God's holy people will receive the kingdom. It will be theirs forever and ever."

decisions.choice: the holy ones of the Most High: God's faithful people, or heavenly beings, or both
decisions.reason: "Holy ones" usually means angels in the Bible and in this book (4:10, 14, 20; 8:13), and some read the phrase so here, with the people of God sharing in their victory (verse 27). But the holy ones are persecuted and worn down by the small horn (verses 21, 25), which fits God's people on earth better, and verse 27 gives the kingdom to "the people of the holy ones". Most readers take the holy ones to be faithful Israel, God's people, perhaps with their angelic champions in view. The text does not settle it.

decisions.choice: the Most High: God
decisions.reason: The title is used of God throughout Daniel (3:26; 4:14, 21-22, 29, 31; 7:25). In this phrase (and in verses 22, 25 and 27) the word has a plural form, probably a plural of majesty, as the Hebrew word for God is plural in form. It means God alone.

decisions.choice: forever, and forever and ever: for all time, with no end
decisions.reason: The phrase repeats "forever" and then strengthens it, so as to say that this kingdom, unlike the four, will never end (2:44; 7:14).

decisions.choice: God's holy people (R)
decisions.reason: The table for Daniel gives "the holy ones of the Most High" at Literal and Balanced and "God's holy people" at Readable. Readable takes the reading that the holy ones are God's faithful people on earth, which verses 21, 25 and 27 favor; the other reading (heavenly beings) is given in the meaning decision at verse 18.

records.source: אֱדַ֗יִן צְבִית֙ לְיַצָּבָ֔א עַל־חֵֽיוְתָא֙ רְבִיעָ֣יְתָ֔א דִּֽי־הֲוָ֥ת שָֽׁנְיָ֖ה מִן־כָּלְּהֵ֑ין דְּחִילָ֣ה יַתִּ֗ירָה שִׁנַּ֤הּ דִּֽי־פַרְזֶל֙ וְטִפְרַ֣יהּ דִּֽי־נְחָ֔שׁ אָֽכְלָ֣ה מַדֲּקָ֔ה וּשְׁאָרָ֖א בְּרַגְלַ֥יהּרָֽפְסָֽה׃
records.gloss: Then I wished to make certain concerning the beast the fourth, which was different from all of them, dreadful exceedingly, its teeth [were] of iron and its claws of bronze, [which was] devouring, crushing, and the rest with its feet trampling;
pieces: Then I wanted to know what the fourth beast meant, the one that was different from all the others and so terrifying, with its iron teeth and bronze claws, that devoured and crushed its victims and trampled what was left under its feet.

L.19: Then I wanted to know the truth about the fourth beast, which was different from all the others, exceedingly dreadful, with its teeth of iron and its claws of bronze, which devoured and crushed and trampled what was left with its feet;

R.19: Then I wanted to know more about the fourth animal. It was different from all the others and very terrifying. It had teeth made of iron and claws made of bronze. It ate and crushed its victims and stamped on whatever was left.

decisions.choice: I wanted to know the truth: the sentence runs on into verse 20
decisions.reason: Daniel asks about the fourth beast, the ten horns and the other horn, and the question runs from verse 19 into verse 20. The verse adds a detail not given in verse 7: the beast had claws of bronze.

records.source: וְעַל־קַרְנַיָּ֤א עֲשַׂר֙ דִּ֣י בְרֵאשַׁ֔הּ וְאָחֳרִי֙ דִּ֣י סִלְקַ֔ת וּנְפַ֥לָה מִן־קֳדָמַ֖הּ תְּלָ֑ת וְקַרְנָ֨א דִכֵּ֜ן וְעַיְנִ֣ין לַ֗הּ וְפֻם֙ מְמַלִּ֣ל רַבְרְבָ֔ן וְחֶזְוַ֖הּ רַ֥ב מִן־חַבְרָתַֽהּ׃
records.gloss: and concerning the horns ten that [were] on its head, and the other that came up, and fell from before it three, and the horn that, and eyes [were] to it, and a mouth speaking great [things], and its appearance [was] greater than its companions.
pieces: I wanted to know as well about the ten horns on its head, and about the other horn that came up, when three of them fell before it. That horn had eyes and a mouth that spoke boastfully, and it looked more imposing than the others.

L.20: and about the ten horns on its head, and about the other one that came up, before which three fell: the horn that had eyes and a mouth speaking great things, and whose appearance was greater than its companions.

R.20: I also asked about the ten horns on its head, and about the other horn that came up. Three of the horns fell in front of it. That horn had eyes and a mouth that was boasting. It looked greater than the other horns.

decisions.choice: whose appearance was greater than its companions: it looked larger than the other horns
decisions.reason: In verse 8 the horn was small when it came up; now it looks greater than the rest. It grows in power, as the small horn of 8:9 grows great.

decisions.choice: I also wanted to know about (B, R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable repeat the verb from verse 19, where Literal continues the sentence.

records.source: חָזֵ֣ה הֲוֵ֔ית וְקַרְנָ֣א דִכֵּ֔ן עָבְדָ֥ה קְרָ֖ב עִם־קַדִּישִׁ֑ין וְיָכְלָ֖ה לְהֽוֹן׃
records.gloss: Seeing I was, and the horn this [was] making war with [the] holy ones, and prevailing against them,
pieces: As I watched, this horn was waging war against the holy ones and was defeating them,

L.21: I kept looking, and this horn was making war with the holy ones and was prevailing against them,

R.21: As I watched, this horn was fighting against God's holy people and was defeating them.

decisions.choice: the horn made war with the holy ones and prevailed: Revelation 13:7
decisions.reason: Revelation 13:7 says of the beast from the sea that it was allowed to make war on the saints and to conquer them, in the words of this verse. Here the holy ones are those whom the horn can attack and defeat, which suits God's people on earth (see verse 18).

decisions.choice: prevailing ... until: the war goes on until the Ancient of Days comes
decisions.reason: The sentence runs on into verse 22. The horn's victories last only until God's judgment is given.

decisions.choice: God's holy people (R)
decisions.reason: The table for Daniel gives "the holy ones of the Most High" at Literal and Balanced and "God's holy people" at Readable. Readable takes the reading that the holy ones are God's faithful people on earth, which verses 21, 25 and 27 favor; the other reading (heavenly beings) is given in the meaning decision at verse 18.

records.gloss: until that came the ancient of days, and the judgment was given for [the] holy ones of [the] Most High, and the time arrived, and the kingdom the holy ones possessed.
pieces: until the Ancient of Days came and gave judgment in favor of the holy ones of the Most High. Then the time came for the holy ones to take possession of the kingdom.

L.22: until the Ancient of Days came, and judgment was given for the holy ones of the Most High, and the time arrived, and the holy ones took possession of the kingdom.

R.22: Then the Ancient One came and judged in favor of God's holy people. The time came for them to receive the kingdom.

decisions.choice: judgment was given for the holy ones: the verdict went in their favor
alternatives: the power of judgment was given to the holy ones
decisions.reason: The phrase can mean that judgment was given in favor of the holy ones (their cause was upheld), or that the right to judge was given to them. The first fits the court scene of verses 9-10 and 26, in which God's court judges. Some read the second, comparing Revelation 20:4, where those seated on thrones are given authority to judge.

decisions.choice: the time arrived: the time God had appointed
decisions.reason: The word is the one for an appointed time. The holy ones receive the kingdom not by their own victory but when God's time comes.

decisions.choice: God's holy people (R)
decisions.reason: The table for Daniel gives "the holy ones of the Most High" at Literal and Balanced and "God's holy people" at Readable. Readable takes the reading that the holy ones are God's faithful people on earth, which verses 21, 25 and 27 favor; the other reading (heavenly beings) is given in the meaning decision at verse 18.

records.gloss: Thus he said: The beast the fourth, a kingdom fourth will be on the earth, which will be different from all the kingdoms, and it will devour all the earth, and will trample it and crush it.
pieces: He said this to me: "The fourth beast is a fourth kingdom that will rise on earth. It will be different from all the other kingdoms. It will devour the whole earth, trampling it down and crushing it.

L.23: Thus he said: "The fourth beast will be a fourth kingdom on the earth, which will be different from all the kingdoms; and it will devour the whole earth, and trample it down and crush it.

R.23: The heavenly being explained, "The fourth animal is a fourth kingdom that will come on the earth. It will be different from all the other kingdoms. It will destroy the whole world. It will stamp on it and crush it.

decisions.choice: the fourth beast will be a fourth kingdom: the beasts are kingdoms as well as kings
decisions.reason: In verse 17 the beasts were four kings; here the fourth is a kingdom. The king stands for his realm. On which kingdom is meant, see verse 17.

decisions.choice: the whole earth: the whole known world
decisions.reason: The phrase is a way of speaking about a world empire, as Nebuchadnezzar's rule reached "to the end of the earth" (4:19).

decisions.choice: The heavenly being explained (R)
decisions.reason: Readable says who is speaking (verse 16).

records.source: וְקַרְנַיָּ֣א עֲשַׂ֔ר מִנַּהּ֙ מַלְכוּתָ֔ה עַשְׂרָ֥ה מַלְכִ֖ין יְקֻמ֑וּן וְאָחֳרָ֞ן יְק֣וּם אַחֲרֵיה֗וֹן וְה֤וּא יִשְׁנֵא֙ מִן־קַדְמָיֵ֔א וּתְלָתָ֥ה מַלְכִ֖ין יְהַשְׁפִּֽל׃
records.gloss: And the horns ten: from it, the kingdom, ten kings will arise; and another will arise after them, and he will be different from the former, and three kings he will bring low.
pieces: The ten horns are ten kings who will arise from this kingdom. After them another king will arise, different from the earlier ones, and he will bring down three kings.

L.24: As for the ten horns, out of this kingdom ten kings will arise; and another will arise after them, and he will be different from the former ones, and he will bring low three kings.

R.24: The ten horns are ten kings who will come from this kingdom. After them another king will come. He will be different from the kings before him. He will defeat three of the kings.

decisions.choice: ten kings, and another after them who brings down three: identified in different ways
decisions.reason: The ten horns are kings who come from the fourth kingdom. In the reading that takes it as Greece, they are kings of the Seleucid line or of the Greek kingdoms before Antiochus IV, and the three he brings down are rivals for the throne in his rise to power in 175 BC. In the reading that takes the kingdom as Rome, they are later rulers, and the last king a final enemy of God. Ten may also be a round number for a full line of kings. The text names none of them.

decisions.choice: bring down (B); defeat (R)
decisions.reason: The verb means to humble or bring low. Balanced keeps the picture; Readable says what it means for a king.

records.source: וּמִלִּ֗ין לְצַ֤ד עִלָּאָה֙ יְמַלִּ֔ל וּלְקַדִּישֵׁ֥י עֶלְיוֹנִ֖ין יְבַלֵּ֑א וְיִסְבַּ֗ר לְהַשְׁנָיָה֙ זִמְנִ֣ין וְדָ֔ת וְיִתְיַהֲב֣וּן בִּידֵ֔הּ עַד־עִדָּ֥ן וְעִדָּנִ֖ין וּפְלַ֥ג עִדָּֽן׃
records.gloss: And words against [the] side of the Most High he will speak, and the holy ones of [the] Most High he will wear out, and he will think to change times and law; and they will be given into his hand until a time and times and half a time.
pieces: He will speak against the Most High and wear down the holy ones of the Most High. He will try to change the sacred times and the law, and they will be handed over to him for a time, two times and half a time.

L.25: He will speak words against the Most High, and he will wear out the holy ones of the Most High, and he will intend to change times and law; and they will be given into his hand for a time, times, and half a time.

R.25: He will speak against the Most High. He will make life very hard for God's holy people. He will try to change their holy days and their laws. God's people will be put under his power for three and a half periods of time.

decisions.choice: wear out: harass and oppress over a long time
decisions.reason: The verb is used of clothes that wear out with long use. The king will grind God's people down by long persecution.

decisions.choice: change times and law: alter the sacred calendar and God's law
decisions.reason: "Times" here are the appointed times, the festivals and sabbaths, and "law" is the religious law that governs them. In the reading that sees Antiochus IV in this king, it fits his ban on the sabbath, the festivals and circumcision in 167 BC, which 1 Maccabees 1:41-50 records. The text speaks only of his intention: God remains the one who "changes times and seasons" (2:21).

decisions.choice: a time, times and half a time: three and a half periods, usually taken as three and a half years
decisions.reason: "Times" is plural and is usually read as two, making three and a half "times" in all, half of seven. The same period comes in 12:7, and Revelation gives it as "a time, and times, and half a time" (Revelation 12:14), as 42 months and as 1,260 days (Revelation 11:2-3; 12:6; 13:5). Half of seven speaks of a time of suffering that is cut short. Whether the "times" are years is not stated, as it is not for the "seven times" of 4:13, 20, 22, 29.

decisions.choice: they will be given into his hand: the holy ones, or the times and law
decisions.reason: "They" most naturally means the holy ones, handed over to his power for a limited time. It could also mean the times and the law, which he will be allowed to change. The first is taken here, as in verse 21.

decisions.choice: three and a half periods of time (R)
decisions.reason: Readable adds up the phrase (m3) but, as in 4:13 ("seven periods of time"), does not say how long a "time" is. Literal and Balanced keep "a time, times and half a time" (Balanced says "two times" for the plural). Reading the plural as two is the usual reading, not a certain one, so this is marked uncertain.

decisions.choice: God's holy people (R)
decisions.reason: The table for Daniel gives "the holy ones of the Most High" at Literal and Balanced and "God's holy people" at Readable. Readable takes the reading that the holy ones are God's faithful people on earth, which verses 21, 25 and 27 favor; the other reading (heavenly beings) is given in the meaning decision at verse 18. Readable says "holy days" for the appointed times (m2).

records.source: וְדִינָ֖א יִתִּ֑ב וְשָׁלְטָנֵ֣הּ יְהַעְדּ֔וֹן לְהַשְׁמָדָ֥ה וּלְהוֹבָדָ֖ה עַד־סוֹפָֽא׃
records.gloss: And the court will sit, and his dominion they will remove, to annihilate and to destroy until the end.
pieces: But the court will sit in judgment, and his authority will be taken away, to be completely and finally destroyed.

L.26: But the court will sit, and his dominion will be taken away, to be annihilated and destroyed to the end.

R.26: But then the court will meet to judge him. His power will be taken away from him, and he will be destroyed completely and forever.

decisions.choice: the court will sit: the heavenly court of verse 10
decisions.reason: The judgment Daniel saw in verses 9-11 is now explained: the small horn's power is taken from him. The plural verb "they will remove", with no subject, means that it will be taken away.

decisions.choice: to annihilate and destroy to the end: to destroy completely
decisions.reason: The two verbs are paired for force, and "to the end" means utterly and for good.

decisions.choice: completely and finally destroyed (B); destroyed completely and forever (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the pair of verbs and "to the end" mean together (m2).

records.source: וּמַלְכוּתָ֨ה וְשָׁלְטָנָ֜א וּרְבוּתָ֗א דִּ֚י מַלְכְוָת֙ תְּח֣וֹת כָּל־שְׁמַיָּ֔א יְהִיבַ֕ת לְעַ֖ם קַדִּישֵׁ֣י עֶלְיוֹנִ֑ין מַלְכוּתֵהּ֙ מַלְכ֣וּת עָלַ֔ם וְכֹל֙ שָׁלְטָ֣נַיָּ֔א לֵ֥הּ יִפְלְח֖וּן וְיִֽשְׁתַּמְּעֽוּן׃
records.gloss: And the kingdom and the dominion and the greatness of the kingdoms under all the heavens was given to [the] people of [the] holy ones of [the] Most High; its kingdom [is] a kingdom of perpetuity, and all the dominions to it will serve and will obey.
pieces: Then the kingdom and the authority and the greatness of all the kingdoms under heaven will be given to the people of the holy ones of the Most High. Their kingdom will last forever, and every ruler will serve and obey them."

L.27: And the kingship and the dominion and the greatness of the kingdoms under all the heavens will be given to the people of the holy ones of the Most High; its kingdom is an everlasting kingdom, and all the dominions will serve and obey it."

R.27: Then the power and greatness of all the kingdoms in the world will be given to the people who belong to the Most High, {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} holy people. Their kingdom will last forever, and all rulers will serve them and obey them."

decisions.choice: was given: will surely be given
decisions.reason: The verb is in the past tense, a way of speaking of what is certain to come as if it had already happened. The verses around it speak of the future.

decisions.choice: the people of the holy ones of the Most High: God's people, who are the holy ones, or the people who belong to the holy ones
decisions.reason: The phrase may mean the people made up of the holy ones, that is, God's holy people; or the people under the protection of the holy ones, the angels. The kingdom given to the one like a son of man in verse 14 is given here to this people. See verse 18.

decisions.choice: its kingdom ... serve and obey it: the people's kingdom, or the Most High's
alternatives: his kingdom is an everlasting kingdom, and all dominions will serve and obey him (the Most High)
decisions.reason: The pronoun is singular. It may refer to the people, the nearest group noun, whose kingdom will never end, as the kingdom of the one like a son of man never ends (verse 14). It may instead refer to the Most High, the last word before it: "his kingdom is an everlasting kingdom, and all dominions will serve and obey him". The verb "serve" is the one used for serving God (see verse 14), which favors the second reading for some. The first is taken here, because the sentence is about the kingdom being given to the people, as in verse 14.

decisions.choice: their, them (B, R) for the singular pronoun
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the singular, "its", for the people. Balanced and Readable say "their" and "them", since a people is many persons; the Aramaic is singular (m3).

decisions.choice: the people who belong to the Most High, his holy people (R)
decisions.reason: Readable takes the first reading of m2, as it does for "the holy ones" (verse 18), and says it plainly. "His" here is the Most High's and stands inside the sentence; it is God's pronoun.

records.source: עַד־כָּ֖ה סוֹפָ֣א דִֽי־מִלְּתָ֑א אֲנָ֨ה דָֽנִיֵּ֜אל שַׂגִּ֣יא׀רַעְיוֹנַ֣י יְבַהֲלֻנַּ֗נִי וְזִיוַי֙ יִשְׁתַּנּ֣וֹן עֲלַ֔י וּמִלְּתָ֖א בְּלִבִּ֥י נִטְרֵֽת׃פ
records.gloss: Until here [is] the end of the matter. I, Daniel, greatly my thoughts alarmed me, and my brightness changed on me, and the matter in my heart I kept.
pieces: This is the end of the account. As for me, Daniel, my thoughts terrified me, and the color drained from my face, but I kept the matter to myself.

L.28: Thus far is the end of the matter. As for me, Daniel, greatly did my thoughts alarm me, and my color changed, but I kept the matter in my heart.

R.28: That is the end of the vision. I, Daniel, was terrified by my thoughts, and my face turned pale. But I kept these things to myself.

decisions.choice: my brightness changed on me: my face turned pale
decisions.reason: The "brightness" is the color of the face. The same phrase is used of Belshazzar's fear (5:6, 9-10).

decisions.choice: I kept the matter in my heart: I kept it to myself and pondered it
decisions.reason: Daniel does not forget or tell the vision, but holds on to it. Compare Luke 2:19, 51, of Mary.

decisions.choice: the end of the Aramaic part of the book
decisions.reason: This verse closes both the vision and the part of the book written in Aramaic, which began at 2:4. Chapter 8 goes on in Hebrew, to the end of the book.

decisions.choice: the color drained from my face (B); my face turned pale (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "my color changed"; Balanced and Readable say what it means (m1). Readable says "kept these things to myself".
